title: Leaderboard
description:
Write `std::vector<int> topScores(std::vector<int> scores, std::size_t count)` that returns the `count` highest scores, highest first. If there are fewer than `count` scores, return them all (still sorted).

Then write `int rankOf(const std::vector<int>& scores, int score)`: the 1-based position `score` would have on the full leaderboard, where rank 1 is the highest. Equal scores share a rank. (The rank is one more than the number of scores that are strictly higher.)

Use standard algorithms rather than hand-written loops where you can: `std::sort` with `std::greater{}`, `resize`, `std::count_if`.
